title_en: What accompanies the absorbed mind: mental factors in the fine-material, immaterial and supramundane minds

sources_read.markers: Section headed '13. රූපාවචර - අරූපාවචර සිත්වල චෛතසික සංග්‍ර‍හය', with a subsection on supramundane minds; ends chapter 2 ('මෙතෙකින් ද්විතීය පරිච්ඡේදය නිමියේ ය')

summary_en: This concept states which of the 52 mental factors (cetasika) accompany the absorption minds. In the exalted minds (fine-material and immaterial), the 13 general factors and 22 of the 25 beautiful factors can arise; the three abstinences are always absent. In the supramundane minds, the 13 general factors and 23 beautiful factors can arise, but the two 'boundless' factors, compassion and appreciative joy, are absent [C031-P:L41; C031-P:L79; C031-M:L3; C031-M:L11]. At each higher level of absorption one factor drops away (applied thought, then sustained thought, then rapture), and at the fifth level compassion and appreciative joy also leave the exalted minds. This gives 35/34/33/32/30 for the exalted minds and 36/35/34/33/33 for the supramundane minds [C031-P:L63–L69; C031-P:L101–L107; C031-M:L5–L13]. The sources explain the exclusions by the kind of object each mind takes: beings, meditation devices or the unconditioned [C031-P:L75; C031-P:L97; C031-M:L15].

sinhala_explanation.heading: සංග්‍රහ නය යනු කුමක්ද, සහ සොයන්නේ කොතැනින්ද
sinhala_explanation.text: සිත් අසූනවයක් හෝ එකසිය විසිඑකක් අතරින් ඒ ඒ සිතේ යෙදෙන චෛතසික දැක්වීමේ ක්‍රමයට "සංග්‍රහ නය" යැයි කියනු ලැබේ [C031-P:L25]. ලෝකෝත්තර ධ්‍යාන සිත්වල චෛතසික සොයන විට අන්‍යසමාන රාශියෙන් සහ සෝභන රාශියෙන් සෙවිය යුතුය. අකුසල චෛතසික සෝභන සිත්වල නොයෙදෙන නිසා ඒවා ඉවත් කළ යුතුය [C031-P:L33]. ඒ ඒ ධ්‍යාන සිතේ ධ්‍යානාඞ්ගද මතක තබාගත යුතුය. ප්‍රථම ධ්‍යානයේ විතක්ක, විචාර, පීති, සුඛ, එකග්ගතා යන පස ඇත. දුතියේ විචාර, පීති, සුඛ, එකග්ගතා යන සතර ඇත. තතියේ පීති, සුඛ, එකග්ගතා යන තුන ඇත. චතුත්ථයේ සුඛ, එකග්ගතා යන දෙක ඇත. පඤ්චමයේ උපෙක්ඛා, එකග්ගතා යන දෙක ඇත [C031-P:L35]. ලෝකෝත්තර සිත්වල ශීල, සමාධි, ප්‍රඥා යන තුනම බලවත්ව පවතින බවද ප්‍රදීපිකාව කියයි [C031-P:L37].

sinhala_explanation.heading: ලෝකෝත්තර සිත් සතළිසේ චෛතසික: 36, 35, 34, 33, 33
sinhala_explanation.text: ප්‍රථම ධ්‍යාන ලෝකෝත්තර සිත් අටෙහි අන්‍යසමාන 13 සහ සෝභන 25න් අප්‍රමාණ්‍ය දෙක හැර ඉතිරි 23 යෙදේ. එවිට චෛතසික 36ක් වේ. අකුසල 14 සහ අප්‍රමාණ්‍ය 2 යන 16 නොලැබේ [C031-P:L41; C031-M:L13]. දුතිය ධ්‍යානයේ විතර්කය නොයෙදේ, එවිට 35ක් යෙදේ (17ක් නොලැබේ) [C031-P:L45]. තතිය ධ්‍යානයේ විචාරයද නොයෙදේ, එවිට 34ක් යෙදේ (18ක් නොලැබේ) [C031-P:L51]. චතුත්ථ ධ්‍යානයේ පීතියද නොයෙදේ, එවිට 33ක් යෙදේ (19ක් නොලැබේ) [C031-P:L55]. පඤ්චම ධ්‍යානයේ සුඛය වෙනුවට උපෙක්ඛාව යෙදෙන නිසා ගණන චතුත්ථයේ මෙන්ම 33කි (19ක් නොලැබේ) [C031-P:L59; C031-P:L69]. ප්‍රදීපිකාවේ වගුවේ මේ පස 'නය' පසක් ලෙස දැක්වේ [C031-P:L63–L69]. මාර්ගය එකම ප්‍රතිඵලය කෙටියෙන් දෙයි: 36, 35, 34, සහ චතුර්ථ-පඤ්චම සිත් 16ට 33 [C031-M:L13].

sinhala_explanation.heading: මහග්ගත සිත් විසිහතේ චෛතසික: 35, 34, 33, 32, 30
sinhala_explanation.text: මහග්ගත සිත් විසිහතකි (27): රූපාවචර ප්‍රථම, දුතිය, තතිය, චතුත්ථ, පඤ්චම ධ්‍යාන සිත් තුන බැගින් සහ අරූපාවචර පඤ්චම ධ්‍යාන සිත් දොළොස [C031-P:L75]. ප්‍රථම ධ්‍යාන මහග්ගත සිත් තුනෙහි අන්‍යසමාන 13 සහ විරති තුන හැර සෝභන 22 යන 35 යෙදේ. අකුසල 14 සහ විරති 3 යන 17 නොලැබේ [C031-P:L79; C031-M:L5]. දුතියේ විතර්කය නැත, එවිට 34ක් යෙදේ [C031-P:L83]. තතියේ විචාරයද නැත, එවිට 33ක් යෙදේ [C031-P:L87]. චතුත්ථයේ පීතියද නැත, එවිට 32ක් යෙදේ (20ක් නොයෙදේ) [C031-P:L93]. පඤ්චම ධ්‍යාන මහග්ගත සිත් පසළොසෙහි (රූපාවචර 3 සහ අරූපාවචර 12) සුඛය වෙනුවට උපෙක්ඛාව යෙදේ. කරුණා, මුදිතා යන අප්‍රමාණ්‍ය දෙකද නොයෙදේ. එවිට 30ක් යෙදෙන අතර 22ක් නොලැබේ [C031-P:L97; C031-P:L107]. මාර්ගයද අරූපාවචර සිත් පඤ්චම ධ්‍යාන සිත්ම වන බැවින් ඒවායේ රූපාවචර පඤ්චම ධ්‍යානයේ මෙන් චෛතසික 30ම යෙදෙන බව කියයි [C031-M:L7].

sinhala_explanation.heading: විරති නොයෙදෙන්නේ ඇයි, අප්‍රමාණ්‍ය යෙදෙන්නේ කොතැනද
sinhala_explanation.text: ප්‍රදීපිකාවට අනුව මහග්ගත ධ්‍යාන වඩන්නෝ සමාධිය ලබාගැනීම සඳහාම වීර්ය කරති. ඒ සමාධිය භාවනාමය කුසල කර්මයේ ප්‍රතිඵලයකි. ශීලමය පුණ්‍යකර්ම කරන විට ඇතිවන විරති චෛතසික ධ්‍යාන සිත්වල නොලැබෙන්නේ ඒ නිසාය [C031-P:L75]. මාර්ගය වෙනත් හේතුවක් දෙයි: මහද්ගත සිත් කසිණාදිය අරමුණු කොටම උපදින නිසා ඒවායේ විරති නොයෙදේ [C031-M:L15]. සුඛිත හෝ දුක්ඛිත සත්ත්ව ප්‍රඥප්තිය අරමුණු කොට ඇතැම් ධ්‍යාන උපදවාගත හැකිය. එසේ වඩන විට කරුණා, මුදිතා යන අප්‍රමාණ්‍ය දෙකද ලැබේ [C031-P:L75]. උපෙක්ඛාව යෙදෙන සිත්වලින් සුඛිත දුක්ඛිත සත්ත්වයන් අරමුණු කළ නොහැකි නිසා පඤ්චම ධ්‍යානයේ ඒවා නොයෙදේ [C031-P:L97]. ලෝකෝත්තර සිත් නිවන අරමුණු කොට උපදී. අප්‍රමාණ්‍ය චෛතසික උපදින්නේ සත්ත්වයන් අරමුණු කොටය. මේ අරමුණුවල වෙනස නිසා ලෝකෝත්තර සිතේ අප්‍රමාණ්‍ය නූපදී [C031-M:L15].

sinhala_explanation.heading: එකවර යෙදිය හැකි උපරිම හා අවම චෛතසික ගණන
sinhala_explanation.text: මාර්ගයට අනුව එකවර වැඩිම චෛතසික ගණනක් යෙදෙන්නේ ලෝකෝත්තර ප්‍රථම ධ්‍යාන සිත්වලය. කාමාවචර කුසලයේ සාමාන්‍යයෙන් චෛතසික 38ක් යෙදෙන බව කීවද, එහි එකවර යෙදිය හැකි උපරිම ගණන 34කි. අඩුම චෛතසික ගණනක් යෙදෙන්නේ ද්විපඤ්චවිඤ්ඤාණයේය [C031-M:L17]. මේ සංසන්දනය ප්‍රදීපිකාවේ මෙම කොටසේ නැත. මාර්ගයේ ද්විතීය පරිච්ඡේදය මෙතැනින් අවසන් වේ [C031-M:L19].

key_terms.en: mental factor: a quality that arises together with a moment of mind
method of combination: showing which mental factors occur in which minds
the 13 general or 'ethically variable' factors, common to both good and bad minds
the three abstinences: from wrong speech, wrong action and wrong livelihood
key_terms.note: Absent in exalted minds, present in supramundane minds [C031-P:L75; C031-M:L3; C031-M:L11]

key_terms.en: the 'boundless' factors: compassion (karuṇā) and appreciative joy (muditā)
key_terms.note: Absent in supramundane minds and in fifth-absorption minds [C031-P:L41; C031-P:L97; C031-M:L15]

key_terms.en: exalted minds: the fine-material and immaterial absorption minds
absorption factors: applied thought, sustained thought, rapture, happiness, one-pointedness, equanimity
applied thought (directing the mind onto the object) / sustained thought (keeping it there)
key_terms.note: Dropped at the second and third absorptions respectively [C031-P:L45; C031-P:L51]

key_terms.en: meditation device, e.g. a disc of earth or colour, used as an object for absorption
key_terms.note: Margaya's reason for the absence of the abstinences [C031-M:L15]

key_terms.en: the concept of a living being, taken as an object
key_terms.note: The object of compassion and appreciative joy [C031-P:L75]

key_terms.en: the two sets of five sense-consciousnesses (seeing, hearing and so on)

human_interpretation_en.heading: Deepening by letting go, one piece at a time
human_interpretation_en.text: The source shows the deeply settled mind becoming simpler as it deepens. First the effort of putting attention onto something drops away. Then the effort of keeping it there drops away. Then the excited uplift drops away. Finally, even pleasant happiness gives way to a quiet evenness. Nothing new has to be added to go deeper; each step is something released. This is a very concrete picture of what 'settling' means: not a mysterious state, but a mind with fewer things going on in it.

human_interpretation_en.heading: Good qualities each have their own occasion
human_interpretation_en.text: Not every good quality is present in every good moment. The quality of restraint, not lying, not harming and not cheating, belongs to moments of actual conduct, when there is something to refrain from. It is not present while the mind rests on a simple meditation object. Compassion and gladness for others need a living being to be about. When the mind rests on something that is not a being, they do not arise, and that says nothing about whether the person is kind. The source is careful to say that a good quality is missing because it has no object, not because it is lacking in the person.

human_interpretation_en.heading: The fullest moment
human_interpretation_en.text: One source says the moment with the most good qualities active at once is the first moment of breakthrough at the first level of settledness. Every kind of restraint, clarity and steadiness is present together there, which ordinary good moments cannot hold all at once. The image is of a moment that is rich rather than empty: peace as completeness, not as blankness.

does_not_transfer: It is not 'meditation makes you a better person automatically'. The source says the abstinences (restraint in speech, action and livelihood) are absent in absorption minds, and places moral restraint elsewhere [C031-P:L75; C031-M:L15].
It is not 'deep states are beyond compassion', and it does not rank compassion lower. Compassion is absent in some minds only because those minds are not directed at beings [C031-P:L97; C031-M:L15].

'Less is more' or 'empty your mind' slogans miss the structure. The drop-outs follow a precise order tied to absorption factors, and the richest moment (36 factors) is also one of the most refined [C031-M:L17].
Focus in work, sport or productivity apps is not the same as these absorptions. The source describes minds of a different plane, not ordinary concentration.
The numbers are an analytic count used in study, not measurements of experience that a person could feel or report.

story_seeds.seed: A master craftsperson doing very fine work over a long session, as talk and fuss fall away and the work narrows to hand, tool and material.
story_seeds.what_camera_could_observe: The first hour of chatting, checking and adjusting. Then long stretches of silence. Breathing slows, the body stills, and the process gets fewer and fewer movements. Afterwards the craftsperson describes the stages in their own words.
story_seeds.why_it_fits: It is a loose parallel. The source shows deepening as successive letting-go: applied thought, sustained thought, rapture, then happiness giving way to evenness [C031-P:L45–L59]. Craft focus is not absorption, and the film should not claim it is. It only lets the audience feel 'deepening by subtraction'.
story_seeds.setting_type: A gem-cutting, jewellery or lacquer workshop in a town known for a traditional craft
story_seeds.risk: It could overclaim a spiritual state for ordinary skilled work, or aestheticise poorly paid labour.

story_seeds.seed: A young monastic's day, where moments of restraint in conduct and moments of seated stillness happen at different times.
story_seeds.what_camera_could_observe: Declining an offered item that the rules forbid, not eating after midday, a careful word in a disagreement, and then separately a long sitting session in a shaded hall.
story_seeds.why_it_fits: The source treats restraint (abstinence) as belonging to the moral side of life and says it is absent in absorption minds [C031-P:L75; C031-M:L15]. The day shows the two as distinct occasions.
story_seeds.setting_type: A village temple or forest monastery
story_seeds.risk: The film must not stage 'restraint' moments or put a novice under pressure to perform piety. Filming minors needs consent from guardians and the institution.

story_seeds.seed: Monks or lay meditators preparing a meditation device, such as a smoothed earth disc or a coloured circle, and then practising with it.
story_seeds.what_camera_could_observe: Mixing clay, shaping and smoothing the disc, choosing where to place it, the first gazing sessions, and the teacher's instructions about distance and posture.
story_seeds.why_it_fits: Margaya explains the absence of restraint factors in absorption minds by saying these minds take meditation devices and similar things as their object [C031-M:L15]. This is the physical object the teaching refers to.
story_seeds.setting_type: A forest hermitage or rural meditation centre
story_seeds.risk: It could treat a living practice as an exotic spectacle, or imply that the people filmed reach absorption. Their own description of what they do must lead.

story_seeds.seed: Someone who divides their life between long periods of solitary quiet and hands-on care for sick or grieving people.
story_seeds.what_camera_could_observe: Early-morning solitary sitting, then the same person at a bedside or with a bereaved family. The different way they hold themselves in each setting, and what they say about moving between the two.
story_seeds.why_it_fits: The source says compassion and appreciative joy arise only when the mind takes beings as its object, not when it rests on a device or on the unconditioned [C031-P:L75; C031-M:L15]. The seed shows the same person's care switching on in the presence of others.
story_seeds.setting_type: A monastic or lay community that runs elder care, a hospice or hospital visits
story_seeds.risk: There is a high risk of exploiting suffering. The film needs strict consent from patients and families, should film the carer rather than the patient's distress, and must not use the sick as illustrations.

story_seeds.seed: A drum ensemble rehearsing, from a single drummer to the moment the whole group plays together at full density.
story_seeds.what_camera_could_observe: Instruments joining one by one, and the peak passage where every part is sounding at once in tight coordination. A lead drummer explains which parts may never play together.
story_seeds.why_it_fits: It is a loose parallel. Margaya notes that some moments hold far more factors at once than others (36 in the first supramundane absorption, at most 34 in ordinary wholesome moments, the fewest in bare sense consciousness) [C031-M:L17]. The ensemble shows 'how many parts can sound together' as something concrete. Its connection to the doctrine is only structural.
story_seeds.setting_type: A village drumming school or temple festival troupe
story_seeds.risk: It is the weakest link to the doctrine and could become a forced analogy. It stands only if the drummers' own story carries the film.

cross_source_notes: The numbers agree fully. Exalted minds: 35/34/33/32/30 [C031-P:L103–L107; C031-M:L5]. Supramundane minds: 36/35/34/33/33 [C031-P:L65–L69; C031-M:L13].

Order differs: Pradeepika treats the supramundane minds first (L27–L69) and then the exalted minds (L73–L107). Margaya treats the exalted minds first (L3–L7) and then the supramundane minds (L9–L17). The Pradeepika header explains that the supramundane method is included because it parallels the exalted method [C031-P:L12].

The reason for the absence of the abstinences in exalted minds differs. Pradeepika says absorption is the fruit of meditative (bhāvanā) merit, while the abstinences arise in moral (sīla) merit [C031-P:L75]. Margaya says exalted minds take meditation devices (kasiṇa) and similar things as object [C031-M:L15]. These two reasons are complementary but not identical; keep both.

The reason for the absence of compassion and appreciative joy in supramundane minds is stated only by Margaya: those minds take the unconditioned as object, whereas compassion and appreciative joy take beings [C031-M:L15]. Pradeepika lists the exclusion [C031-P:L41] without giving a reason in this extract.

Pradeepika alone lists the absorption factors in the fivefold scheme [C031-P:L35], says that virtue, concentration and wisdom are all strong in supramundane minds [C031-P:L37], and gives the 'not obtained' count for each level. Margaya alone gives the comparison of maximum and minimum (36 in the first supramundane absorption, at most 34 at once in sense-sphere wholesome minds, the fewest in the sense consciousnesses) [C031-M:L17].
Margaya numbers this section '13.' within its chapter 2 [C031-M:L1]; this is the book's own numbering, unrelated to the project's Concept 31.
uncertainties: Pradeepika's table computes the supramundane fifth absorption as '33 minus happiness = 32, plus equanimity 1 = 33' [C031-P:L69], and the exalted fifth absorption as 'happiness replaced by equanimity' [C031-P:L107]. Both happiness and equanimity here are forms of the single feeling factor, so the net count is unchanged. On screen, this must not be presented as a separate factor being added.
The Pradeepika extract ends on the pdf 209 page marker with no text after it [C031-P:L109]. Any closing remarks on pdf 209 (for example, summary verses) are not included.

The Pradeepika extract begins mid-page on pdf 204 [C031-P:L21]. The listing of the 52 factors and the definitions of the 13 general and 25 beautiful factors lie outside this extract, so the total of 52 is only implied by the arithmetic here.

Margaya's claim that sense-sphere wholesome minds can hold at most 34 factors at once, even though 38 are listed for them [C031-M:L17], is not explained in the extract. The usual explanation (the abstinences and the boundless factors arise only one at a time, and never together, in mundane minds) needs to be confirmed from another section before use.

Pradeepika says only 'some' absorptions are developed with beings as object and so include compassion and appreciative joy [C031-P:L75]. The '35' for the first exalted absorption is therefore a maximum of possible factors, not a claim that all 35 are present in every such moment. An expert should confirm how to phrase this.
Minor typographic issues: a missing full stop at L29 ('අටෙකි'), 'යෙදෙන් නාහ' split at L93, and 'යෙදෙනේනේ' at C031-M:L7. None of these affect the meaning.
evidence_class_note: sinhala_explanation and summary_en = source teaching; human_interpretation_en and story_seeds = editorial interpretation; nothing here is documentary evidence.
